Primary failure mode setting upper bound: Balance element; practical simplex / leaving Al-rich CALPHAD region if too low
Notes / caveats: Use Al as balance with an explicit Al_min = 85 wt%. This keeps BOFN in the Al-rich TCAl10/Muggianu region while still allowing up to 15 wt% total solute for k=3..8 active elements.

Primary failure mode setting upper bound: Mn-rich intermetallic precipitation / loss of metastable supersaturation
Notes / caveats: 5.0 wt% because LPBF evidence supports it, it covers the Al-Mn-Cr-Zr anchor family, and simplex + Mn+Cr joint constraints stop pathological combined loading. The 0.05–0.10 wt% activity floor is enough when Mn is on.

Primary failure mode setting upper bound: Primary Al-Cr intermetallic formation and narrowed LPBF process window
Notes / caveats: The per-element file allowed up to 6 wt% Cr, but the joint synthesis pulled this back to 3 wt% to stay in a more credible TCAl10 region and reduce risk of coarse Al₅Cr/Al₇Cr phases.

Primary failure mode setting upper bound: Primary Al₃Zr formation / coarsening and porosity sensitivity
Notes / caveats: 1 wt% is the practical BOFN cap. It captures the grain-refining benefit seen in LPBF without leaning too hard on poorly assessed high-Zr corners. If Sc and Zr are both active, treat 0.2 wt% each as a practical minimum and enforce Sc+Zr ≤ 1.5 wt% conservatively.

Primary failure mode setting upper bound: Evaporation / spatter / composition drift plus hot cracking
Notes / caveats: 8 wt% Mg has been printed in tailored systems, but evaporation is already serious there. For BOFN, 5 wt% is the cleaner choice because it respects LPBF transfer-function reality and avoids spending too much search volume on Mg-burnoff corners. Consider joint cap Mg+Zn+Li ≤ 10 wt%.

Primary failure mode setting upper bound: Transition to hypereutectic behavior with primary Si precipitation
Notes / caveats: 12 wt% captures the eutectic Al-Si printable regime and the main crack-mitigation role of Si. Going higher trades BOFN volume toward coarse primary Si and stronger process sensitivity. If Si is active for crack suppression, a functional floor around 3–4 wt% is defensible.

Primary failure mode setting upper bound: Wide freezing range / solidification cracking and θ-Al₂Cu segregation
Notes / caveats: For a single shared search space 4 wt% is the safer BOFN choice because Cu strongly worsens cracking in broad Al-rich multicomponent regions and also carries mineral-burden penalty. Enforce Cu+Mg ≤ 5 wt% conservatively.
Used the joint conservative value. Higher Ti only makes sense on a specific Ti-B manifold; otherwise it mostly creates Al₃Ti risk and atomization trouble. Literature is conditional rather than broad.

Primary failure mode setting upper bound: Brittle Fe-rich intermetallics especially β-Al₅FeSi-type morphologies
Notes / caveats: The per-element file noted 5 wt% Fe in dedicated high-temperature Al-Fe-Cr systems, but the joint synthesis reduced Fe to 0.5 wt% for a general BOFN space. If Fe is intentionally elevated above 0.3 wt%, use Mn to redirect phase morphology and watch Fe+Si.

Primary failure mode setting upper bound: Brittle Al-Ni intermetallic networks and cracking
Notes / caveats: Per-element Ni had a eutectic-targeted non-conservative ceiling around 5.7 wt%, but for the shared BOFN space 0.5 wt% is the better recommendation. Ni also adds mineral-burden cost and has thin evidence outside targeted eutectic designs.

Primary failure mode setting upper bound: Primary Al₁₁Ce₃ and Ce-rich network formation
Notes / caveats: The per-element file went as high as 10–15 wt% Ce in near-eutectic systems. 6 wt% for BOFN preserves access to Ce-containing discovery space without overcommitting to rare-earth-heavy oxidation-sensitive corners. Pre-alloyed feedstock is preferred over elemental blending.

Primary failure mode setting upper bound: Cost/criticality plus primary Al₃(Sc,Zr) formation that wastes solute
Notes / caveats: 0.8 wt% matches Scalmalloy-class practice and is the obvious BOFN cap. Higher Sc quickly becomes a mineral-burden loser and starts consuming Sc in primary phases rather than useful nano-precipitates.

Primary failure mode setting upper bound: Evaporation / atmosphere sensitivity and δ′(Al₃Li)-related embrittlement
Notes / caveats: Kept the joint conservative value. LPBF at 3 wt% Li exists, but density penalties and Li loss are already substantial. Candidate for explicit transfer-function correction if BOFN insists on exploring it.

Primary failure mode setting upper bound: Al₃Er intermetallic formation / coarsening; poor general LPBF robustness outside targeted eutectics
Notes / caveats: Per-element Er had a very high non-conservative ceiling in near-eutectic Al-Er concepts, but the evidence for broad use is thin. For BOFN, 0.5 wt% is the defensible cap. Treat higher Er as a follow-up branch, not default search volume.

Primary failure mode setting upper bound: Zn evaporation / composition drift plus hot cracking in Al-Zn-Mg corridors
Notes / caveats: Per-element work found 6.5 wt% conservative and 14.5 wt% non-conservative; the non-conservative ceiling is capped at 15 wt% because the simplex constraint with Al_min = 85 wt% caps any single non-Al element at 15 wt%. 8 wt% preserves 7xxx-like exploration but avoids dedicating too much search to Zn-loss-dominated space. Enforce volatile-elements cap Mg+Zn+Li ≤ 10 wt% conservatively.

Primary failure mode setting upper bound: Monotectic immiscibility and low-melting Sn-rich grain-boundary films
Notes / caveats: Keep Sn near trace level in the default BOFN space. The per-element file had a much larger exploratory ceiling under the project's Al-rich constraint, but the LPBF evidence is thin and failure modes are significant.
